text: The model has classified the brain MRI as "No Tumour", meaning it did not detect imaging features that match the three tumour types it was trained on - glioma, meningioma or pituitary tumour [neurasight-system]. This is a classification output, not a diagnostic conclusion, and it does not equate to a normal scan or a clean bill of health. The system only recognises four categories; other abnormalities such as infarction, haemorrhage, infection or developmental lesions lie outside its experience and may be assigned to the "No Tumour" class by default [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. Likewise, the absence of a detected tumour does not guarantee the absence of disease, a single slice does not represent the whole study, and clinical correlation remains essential [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. If the patient has any concerning symptoms - for example sudden severe headache, new seizures, loss of consciousness, focal weakness, visual change, confusion or persistent vomiting - these should prompt prompt medical assessment regardless of the classification [ninds-brain-tumors]. In such circumstances it would be appropriate to discuss with a qualified clinician a thorough neurological examination, a formal radiological report of the complete imaging set, possible repeat or additional imaging with full coverage, evaluation for non-tumour causes of the symptoms and referral to a specialist if needed [nci-cns-pdq-patient] [ninds-brain-tumors].
